title: Release train choreography and contingency thresholds for API, Console & Runtime launch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a practical, testable release train plan that locks scope, defines numeric cut/rollback thresholds, sequences cross-team deliverables, and coordinates release notes and GTM tasks across API, Console, and Runtime teams. This ticket codifies the timeline windows, gating metrics, and contingency playbooks so PM, Eng, Design, and GTM have a single source of truth for the next integrated launch.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone calendar published and accepted by ENG/Design/Sales Engineering leads
Scope freeze date set with explicit allowed exception list and owner signatures
Cut and rollback thresholds documented with numeric values and signal owners
Release notes owner and per-component templates assigned; draft notes submitted two business days before release
Post-launch observability dashboard and playbook created and linked to the runbook

cut_thresholds_and_gates: API availability: abort release if 5m error rate > 1.0% AND sustained for 10 minutes
Latency: abort or rollback if p95 trailing 5m increases by >30% relative to baseline for API or Runtime kernels
KV cache signal: if cache miss rate > 20% AND request amplification observed, trigger immediate throttled rollback for affected shard
Console client regressions: block full rollout if critical E2E flows fail in canary (>2 failing user journeys in smoke test suite)
Observability gap: do not proceed to full rollout if any required dashboards or alerts are not functional and linked in the runbook
canary_and_rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Internal canary (engineering/internal accounts only) for 2 hours
Phase 2 - Small external canary (1% traffic) for 4 hours with automatic monitoring checks
Phase 3 - Ramp to 10% traffic over 3 hours if no gating events
Phase 4 - Full ramp to 100% over 12 hours with staggered region release windows
Rollback ladder - Graceful degrade to fallback model variant, then partial traffic cut back to previous release, then full rollback if metrics persist beyond 30 minutes
release_notes_coordination: Assign component owners: API (Diego Martinez), Console (Priya Nair), Runtime (Lena Cho)
Notes split into Public Summary, Technical Details, Breaking Changes, Upgrade Instructions, and Known Issues
Internal changelog to include runbook links, migration steps, and incident contacts
Final notes draft due 48 hours before M4; release notes PR must be approved by PM + Eng lead
cross_team_gtm_tasks: Sales enablement doc and training session (owner: Sales Eng - Dylan Park)
Customer success playbook with troubleshooting checklist and escalation paths
Marketing launch assets signoff and embargo schedule
Marketplace listing updates and compliance paperwork for Private deployments
Support rotation plan and 24/72 hour response SLAs defined for launch week
observability_and_playbooks: SLOs & thresholds codified (p99 latency, p95 latency, error rate) and linked to alerts
Pre-built Grafana dashboard for release train signals
On-call playbook with owner contact list and rollback steps
Synthetic smoke tests to run automatically during each canary window
notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive ramp improves time-to-value but raises risk of regressions in telemetry-sensitive workloads. We prioritize rollback-first policy for customer-facing errors and graceful fallback for model variants. Key unknowns: quantization compatibility for a subset of runtime models and possible Console bundle regressions after inline analytics change.
